text.content:
Something alive is wearing you, and it grows by eating. Feed it a ruby and it learns to burn; feed it iron and the limbs get heavier; feed it nickel and neither of you knows what you will have on Tuesday. Your build is not a list of choices made at creation. It is a stomach, and its contents are visible on you.

Mechanically: 10 Hit Points per level, expert in all three saves, unarmoured expert, unarmed attacks only — the Carapace Strike (1d8 bludgeoning) — and an Assimilator DC keyed to Strength or Dexterity. Constitution is your most important secondary attribute.

The three things a new player should know

  • Open the Gullet. Everything you have eaten, every choice it asks of you each morning, and the Feed and Shed buttons live in one window: the Open the Gullet macro, or the Feed and Shed actions on your sheet.
  • Depth is the number that matters. Each Substrate's effect shows as a counter on its effect — that is its Depth, 1 to 4 — and every Mutation, Instinct and Bond reads it.
  • The plate can break. Carapace Block turns physical damage with your Hardness and the plate pays for it. A broken Carapace switches off every Mutation at Depth 3 or higher until you mend it.

pages.name: Eating: Mass, Depth and the Gullet

text.content:
You have two pools of Mass, Gem and Metal. A Substrate at Depth N costs N Mass in its own pool. Wide or deep is your call, asked once per pool.

Level135811141720
Gem Mass1235791113
Metal Mass112457810
Depth cap11223344

Feed and Shed

  • Feed (10 minutes) consumes a Substrate you are carrying — a specimen whose name is the Substrate's, like a looted ruby or a copper ingot — and raises that Substrate's Depth by 1 (a new one enters at Depth 1). The Gullet lists the specimens you carry for each. It is refused in an encounter.
  • Depth 3–4 takes a quickened specimen, which only the GM can mark. Ordinary ones stop at Depth 2.
  • The Vein: each time your Mass grows you get one free Substrate — the Gullet offers it as a source.
  • Shed lowers or removes a Substrate, during daily preparations only. What you shed is destroyed.

Every morning

Rest for the Night opens daily preparations in the Gullet. That is when you Shed, break an Instinct tie, change a Bond, and make the day's choices your Substrates and feats ask for (Gold's pick, Electrum's second colour, Zinc's energy type, Nickel's Aberrations, and the rest). Finish preparing settles your Instinct.

• Carapace Strike — unarmed, 1d8 bludgeoning, brawling. Handwraps of Mighty Blows work normally; buy them.
  • Living Plate — your armour, alive: explorer's clothing that takes armour runes. You cannot wear other armour.
  • Hardness 2, plus the highest Hardness bonus among your Substrates (Adamant Shell makes them add), plus the Gray Instinct's. Hit Points 10 + 5 per level; Broken Threshold half of that.
  • Carapace Block (reaction): against physical damage, reduce it by the plate's Hardness; the plate takes that much. Use the action on your sheet to arm it; it answers the next physical blow and is spent.
  • Broken: every Mutation at Depth 3+ switches off, and its actions leave your sheet until the plate is mended. Mend it with the Repair activity, or an hour feeding it a Substrate you don't bind (Mend in the Gullet).

Your Instinct is the colour with the most total Mass, both pools together; ties are yours to break at daily preparations. Its clause applies to every Mutation you have, whatever its colour, and it sets your Instinct's damage type. It moves only at daily preparations (or the first time you bind anything).

Electrum at Depth 3 adds its second colour's clause beside yours, both at half value; at Depth 4 both at full. Two Instincts does the same at half — you get the better of the two, never both.

Thirty-six Substrates, four per colour. Each is an effect whose counter is its Depth; its description lists what every Depth does. Their actions — Flare, Discharge, Shadow Step, Reactive Evolution — appear on your sheet when their Depth is reached.

Bonds

A Bond needs both its Substrates at Depth 2 or higher and a Bond slot (the first at 4th, then 8th, 12th, 16th, 20th). Slot it in the Gullet; it changes only at daily preparations. If either Substrate drops below Depth 2 the Bond is suppressed, not lost, and comes back when you feed it again. Electrum at Depth 2 may stand in for either Substrate of one Bond you name.

pages.name: What the module does, and what it leaves to you

text.content:
Almost everything the class does happens by itself. A few things ask you, and a few are left to the table on purpose.

It happens by itself

  • Every number: Mutations' damage and resistances, Instinct clauses, Bonds, Hardness, fast healing, Speeds.
  • What a Mutation does when it deals damage, when you are hit, at the start of a turn, when you move — Red's bonus, Green's temporary Hit Points, Copper's arcs, Amber's charges, Manganese's corrosion, Molten Carapace's burn.
  • Once-per-encounter and once-per-round limits: a spent action's card is refused with a notice.
  • Areas: Flare, Null Field and the Healing Flare are emanations and need only a Confirm targets click. The Gland's cone and the Discharge's line are aimed: click where the area starts, point the way it faces, click again.

It asks you

  • Cards in chat with buttons: the Black Instinct's check or DC, the White Instinct's ally, Shed Skin, Devouring Plate, Cleansing Light when an ally holds several conditions.
  • Pickers when you use an action: which condition Purify or Cleansing Tide ends, what Devour eats, what Assimilate takes, what Sympathetic Growth shares.
  • Prompts for your choices at the moment they arise: Kinetic Spurs, Battle Frame, Living Armour's Reactive Evolution, Apex Predator's Depth 4 riders.

It leaves to the table

  • Movement it cannot see: teleporting between areas of darkness, hovering, moving through a creature's space, where the Wall of Me stands and the cover it gives.
  • Notes shown on a roll that nothing enforces: a Mutation's situational bonus, a flat check an enemy owes.
  • Rulings: what counts as a corpse or a quickened specimen, and "one of its abilities" from Eat the World.

• Substrates are your lever. The player's build is what they have eaten; what you put in the world decides what they can become. Ordinary specimens are shop goods and loot; quickened ones never are.
  • Marking a quickened specimen. On the item, set the flag flags.isaacs-hb-pf2e.assimilator.specimen = { substrate: "<slug>", quickened: true } — for example { substrate: "ruby", quickened: true }. The Gullet then offers it for Depth 3–4.
  • The Carapace breaking is a scene, not a punishment. A broken plate at 17th loses its Depth 4 riders; give the player a way to mend it that is worth an hour.
  • Feeding happens in downtime. Feed is 10 minutes and is refused in an encounter.
  • Rulings the module took, which you may overrule: Purple's raised Substrate may pass the Depth cap (never above 4); a lowered Depth 1 Substrate does not manifest that day; Mindstorm's stupefied lasts until the end of the creature's next turn; Moonstone's Reactive Evolution is the player's reaction to take.
